name: buttery spirits

attributes.attribute: had a great hunger for butter

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Buttery spirits is a British and Scottish term. It stands for the fairies who stole away butter. Fairies loved rich food. The name gave these spirits a plain household label. The word points to the churning that fairies were said to disrupt.

okr.objective: Introduce buttery spirits as the fairies who stole butter.
key_results: Buttery spirits is a British and Scottish term.
It names fairies who stole away butter.
The name reflects a fairy hunger for rich food.
